description: During epoll_ctl(A, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, B), the nesting-depth check walks A->refs under rcu_read_lock() and follows each epi->ep back-pointer to the watching eventpoll instance. While the epitem list entries are protected by kfree_rcu(), the struct eventpoll they point to is released via plain kfree() in ep_free(). A second thread closing a watcher fd can therefore free that eventpoll while the walker still holds a pointer to it, after which the walker writes loop_check_gen (u64) and loop_check_depth (u8) into freed memory. By spraying the freed kmalloc slot with attacker-controlled data, this becomes a constrained write-what-where primitive; chained with two info leaks, the reporter's PoC overwrites cred->cap_permitted, gains CAP_SYS_MODULE, and loads a kernel module to obtain root in ~20 seconds on a default preempt=voluntary build.
location: ep_get_upwards_depth_proc() in fs/eventpoll.c; ep_free() in fs/eventpoll.c
reproduction: 1. Leak KASLR base and a pointer into current task's struct cred via an io_uring fdinfo OOB read.
2. Leak the kernel address of a kmalloc-192 slot adjacent to a controlled user_key_payload via a keyctl PKEY_ENCRYPT OOB read; stage a fake epitem there.
3. Build a large ep->refs list (~4000 watchers) so the depth-check walk is long; run ~25,000 priming epoll_ctl calls to advance loop_check_gen near a useful value.

4. On CPU 0, repeatedly call epoll_ctl(ADD) to trigger ep_get_upwards_depth_proc(); on CPU 1, close watcher fds to free their struct eventpoll mid-walk; a third thread fires membarrier(PRIVATE_EXPEDITED) IPIs to stall CPU 0 under preempt=voluntary.

5. Immediately spray the freed eventpoll slot with a user_key_payload whose bytes place a pointer to the stage-2 fake at the epi->ep offset; the walker follows it and writes loop_check_gen into what is actually cred->cap_permitted.
6. The next field (cap_effective) is zero and is misread as an empty ep->refs list head, so the walker returns cleanly without crashing.
7. Repeat until a written counter value has bit 16 (CAP_SYS_MODULE) set; call capset() to copy permitted into effective, then finit_module() an embedded module that commits root creds.
technical_details:
Hi --

I believe I've found another local privilege escalation vulnerability

in the kernel. This one requires no special user permissions.

(As in my prior bugs, I used an LLM to find this, but I validated it

myself. The exploit, again, is something I don't *fully* understand,

but I've tried my best to explain whats happening and it's easy to

verify the behavior from input-output testing.)

The vulnerability is in ep_get_upwards_depth_proc(), in

fs/eventpoll.c. This function walks a linked list ep->refs (while

holding rcu_read_lock()) and dereferences epi->ep on each entry:

    static int ep_get_upwards_depth_proc(struct eventpoll *ep, int depth)

    {

        int result = 0;

        struct epitem *epi;

        if (ep->gen == loop_check_gen)

            return ep->loop_check_depth;

        hlist_for_each_entry_rcu(epi, &ep->refs, fllink)

            result = max(result,

                         ep_get_upwards_depth_proc(epi->ep, depth + 1) + 1);

        ep->gen = loop_check_gen;

        ep->loop_check_depth = result;

        return result;

    }

The list entries (struct epitem) are freed via kfree_rcu(), so the

list walk is safe. But epi->ep points at a struct eventpoll, which

is freed by plain kfree() in ep_free() without waiting for the

grace period:

    static void ep_free(struct eventpoll *ep)

    {

        ep_resume_napi_irqs(ep);

        mutex_destroy(&ep->mtx);

        free_uid(ep->user);

        wakeup_source_unregister(ep->ws);

        kfree(ep);                    /* no grace period */

    }

The walk runs when one epoll_ctl(A, EPOLL_CTL_ADD, B) call checks

whether adding B to A's interest list would create deep (or infinite)

nesting. The list being walked is A->refs---the set of epoll

instances that are watching A. Each entry's epi->ep back-pointer names

one of those watchers. If a second thread closes a watcher fd while

the first is mid-walk, ep_free() can kfree() that watcher's struct

eventpoll while the walker still holds a pointer to it. The walker

then writes loop_check_gen (a u64) and loop_check_depth (a u8) into

freed memory.

I think this was introduced by f2e467a48287 ("eventpoll: Fix

semi-unbounded recursion", 2025-07-11), which added this upward

depth check.

The attached repro-2cpu.c is a minimal crasher. One thread on CPU 0

hammers epoll_ctl(ADD) calls, each of which walks a 4000-entry refs list;

a second thread on CPU 1 closes the watchers one by one. Under

preempt=voluntary the walk cannot be scheduler-preempted, but natural

IRQ stalls on CPU 0 give the closer time to free+reallocate the buffer

before the IRQ finishes. Under a KASAN-compiled kernel this reports

slab-use-after-free in a few seconds.

I've also attached a second lpe.c that chains this with two other

info-leak bugs (which I will report separately) to get root on a HEAD

build (as of two days ago---I sent a patch for one of the three bugs

in this chain that recently landed). The attack here has to be a bit

more clever in order to make sure it can abuse the race

productively. The chain works (again, I believe!) as follows:

1. An io_uring fdinfo OOB read leaks KASLR base and a pointer into

   the current task's struct cred. (I have filed this bug already,

   and the fix will be merged. But any other KALSR bypass could

   substitute here.)

2. A keyctl PKEY_ENCRYPT OOB read leaks the address of a

   kmalloc-192 slot adjacent to a controlled user_key_payload.

   This is where we will stage a fake epitem that the walker will

   follow---it has to live in kernel memory so SMAP doesn't kill us.

3. The epoll UAF gives a write-at-chosen-address primitive: when the

   closer thread frees a watcher's struct eventpoll, a spray reclaims

   that slot with a user_key_payload whose data places a pointer to

   our stage-2 fake at the epi->ep offset. The walker follows that

   pointer and writes loop_check_gen at the offset where ep->gen

   would be.

4. The value written is (as mentioned) not controllable. But there are

   places in the kernel where writing *any* value gives power, and the

   PoC targets cred->cap_permitted as one of these.

   This target has a convenient property: in struct cred,

   cap_permitted is immediately followed by cap_effective. For an

   unprivileged task, cap_effective is zero. The walker, after

   writing to cap_permitted, reads what it thinks is ep->refs.first

   at the next offset---which is cap_effective---gets zero,

   interprets that as an empty list, and returns cleanly.

   Roughly half of counter values have bit 16 (CAP_SYS_MODULE) set,

   so after a few writes cap_permitted contains that bit, the

   exploit calls capset() to copy permitted into effective, and

   finit_module() loads a kernel module that commits root creds.

The bulk of the PoC's complexity is in making the race win under

preempt=voluntary, which is the distro default. Under preempt=full the

walker can be scheduler-preempted mid-walk, and then the closer has

all the time in the world to run their exploit. Under a voluntary

scheduler, the walker only yields to IRQs. So the PoC puts the closer

in a separate process on a different CPU and uses membarrier

PRIVATE_EXPEDITED as an IPI gun from a third thread to storm the

walker's CPU with interrupts---stalling it long enough for close+spray

to complete. A "priming" pass that runs 25,000 non-racing epoll_ctl

calls first brings loop_check_gen near the threshold, so the race only

needs to win twice. With these techniques the voluntary version hits

root in ~20 seconds with fairly high reliability.

I've attached a patch that switches ep_free() to kfree_rcu(). This is

the smallest change I could find that fixes the vulnerability, but I

don't know if it's the right change. Feel free to disregard.

Thanks,

Nicholas

Reproduction:

  git clone https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git

  cd linux

  git checkout 5170efd9c344~1

  make defconfig

  scripts/config -e PKCS8_PRIVATE_KEY_PARSER

  make olddefconfig

  make -j$(nproc) bzImage modules

  # Build the embedded kernel module for finit_module (lpe.c embeds the

  # bytes via pwnmod_ko.h, but vermagic must match the kernel you just

  # built):

  mkdir pwnmod && cp pwnmod.c pwnmod/

  echo 'obj-m := pwnmod.o' > pwnmod/Makefile

  make -C . M=$PWD/pwnmod modules

  xxd -i pwnmod/pwnmod.ko | sed 's/pwnmod_pwnmod_ko/pwnmod_ko/' > pwnmod_ko.h

  # Update the io_uring_fops offset in lpe.c for this build:

  FOPS=$(nm vmlinux | awk '/ io_uring_fops$/{print $1}')

  sed -i "s/^#define KSTATIC_IO_URING_FOPS.*/#define

KSTATIC_IO_URING_FOPS  0x${FOPS}UL/" lpe.c

  # Alpine nocloud image + cloud-init seed

  wget https://dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/alpine/v3.23/releases/cloud/nocloud_alpine-3.23.0-x86_64-bios-cloudinit-metal-r0.qcow2

-O alpine.qcow2

  cat > user-data <<'EOF'

  #cloud-config

  disable_root: false

  ssh_pwauth: true

  chpasswd:

    expire: false

    list: |

      root:test

  runcmd:

    - sed -i 's/^#*PermitRootLogin.*/PermitRootLogin yes/' /etc/ssh/sshd_config

    - rc-service sshd restart

  EOF

  printf 'instance-id: x\nlocal-hostname: x\n' > meta-data

  genisoimage -output seed.iso -volid cidata -joliet -rock user-data meta-data

  qemu-img create -f qcow2 -F qcow2 -b alpine.qcow2 disk.qcow2 4G

  qemu-system-x86_64 -enable-kvm -m 2G -smp 4 -nographic \

    -kernel arch/x86/boot/bzImage \

    -append "root=/dev/vda rw console=ttyS0 preempt=voluntary rootwait" \

    -drive file=disk.qcow2,if=virtio \

    -drive file=seed.iso,if=virtio,format=raw \

    -netdev user,id=n0,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 -device virtio-net,netdev=n0

  # on the host (lpe.c needs rsa2048.h and pwnmod_ko.h in the same dir):

  gcc -O2 -static -pthread -o lpe lpe.c

  scp -P 2222 lpe root@localhost:/tmp/     # password 'test'

  # ssh -p 2222 root@localhost

  adduser -D testuser

  su testuser -c "FORCE_2CPU=1 /tmp/lpe"

  # [+] KBASE = 0xffffffff81000000 (io_uring_fops = ...)

  # [+]  K1 @ g_k1_addr=0xffff... via idx=30 (j+4, marker-verified, tried 7)

  # [.] priming loop_check_gen (~50k, 25000 adds)...

  # [.]  r=0 prm=0000e39f/00000000

  # [.]  r=1 prm=00010465/00000000

  # [+++] CAP_SYS_MODULE in permitted! (round 1)

  # [++++++] PWNED -- uid=0 via init_module

  # uid=0(root) gid=0(root)

For the crasher, rebuild with KASAN (scripts/config -e KASAN -e

KASAN_GENERIC, same steps otherwise), scp repro-2cpu, and run it

unprivileged; expect a slab-use-after-free splat in

ep_get_upwards_depth_proc within a few seconds.
title: UAF in ep_get_upwards_depth_proc() giving unprivileged LPE
